Q: How to implement and compare multiple machine learning algorithms (Regression, Classification) in Python using scikit-learn? A:

Generally speaking this is a how most people would implement these algorithms using sci-kit. However, there are few nuances, you should consider while working on these projects. You should evaluate the performance of each algorithm by training and testing on variety of datasets. There are so many open source datasets available for training/testing AI/ML algorithms such as MNIST , etc.. You can find full list of open source datasets here . I have not checked the complete list so I am not sure if they all are annotated or some kind of manual annotation is needed for the some of them.

Regarding performance comparison, there are many metrics that could have been used, such as detection/classification accuracy, precision, F1-score, and area under the ROC curve for classification tasks, as well as mean absolute error (MAE) and mean squared error (MSE) for regression tasks. These metrics help evaluate how well models perform and allow for objective comparisons between different algorithms.

Remember, in AI/ML algorithms rigorous/continuous training and test is the key. More you train, better it would knowledge about its performance, whether it optimally fits, underfits or overfits.

Q: The format of the maven plugins in the pom.xml A:

Plugins go to the `<plugins>` section. You can copy groupId, artifactId and version from some source on the internet, but for the configuration, you need to understand what the plugin should be doing.

Q: 2D fourier transform gone wrong ,where am I wrong? A:

For 2D such as image processing one can do the DFT for each row and column then add the results.

For example if the DFT of row 1 produces 1 and the DFT of column 1 produces 2 then in the 2D DFT the cell at the location of 1,1 will have the value of 1+2=3

That is false. At best, in some very specific cases, you can multiply the DFT of the two axis, but your example is not one of them.

Your best shot at debuging your implementation is to display the results, using pyplot for instance. You'll see immediately what is wrong.

The following code should do what you want, though it simply uses numpy for the 2D DFT.

import re
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

pixel = re.compile(r'\((?P<R>\d{1,3}),(?P<G>\d{1,3}),(?P<B>\d{1,3})\)')

with open('image.txt', 'r') as image_file:
    lines = image_file.readlines()

image = []

for n, line in enumerate(lines):
    image.append([])
    for m in pixel.finditer(line):
        image[n].append(
            [
                int(m.group('R')),
                int(m.group('G')),
                int(m.group('B')),
            ]
        )

image = np.array(image)

image_fft = np.abs(np.fft.fft2(image, axes=(0, 1)))
image_fft = image_fft / image_fft.max()

fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2)
ax1.imshow(image)
ax2.imshow(image_fft)
fig.show()

Q: Inexplicable npm Error with @mui and x-date-pickers A:

This happens when NPM can't decide which version of a package to install, because two dependencies of your project use incompatible versions of a dependency of their own.

In this case, @mui/x-date-pickers@7.27.3 dependes on versions ^5.15 up to ^6 of @mui/material, while in myWebApp you have @mui/material@7.3.4 specified.

To fix this you should find compatible versions. for that you can use for example npm view <package> peerDependencies to find compatible versions.

When you run npm view @mui/x-date-pickers@^8 peerDependencies, i.e next major so likely to support your version of @mui/material, you can see the following output:

8 peerDependencies
@mui/x-date-pickers@8.0.0 {
  dayjs: '^1.10.7',
  luxon: '^3.0.2',
  react: '^17.0.0 || ^18.0.0 || ^19.0.0',
  moment: '^2.29.4',
  'date-fns': '^2.25.0 || ^3.2.0 || ^4.0.0',
  'react-dom': '^17.0.0 || ^18.0.0 || ^19.0.0',
  '@mui/system': '^5.15.14 || ^6.0.0 || ^7.0.0',
  'moment-hijri': '^2.1.2 || ^3.0.0',
  '@mui/material': '^5.15.14 || ^6.0.0 || ^7.0.0',
  '@emotion/react': '^11.9.0',
  'moment-jalaali': '^0.7.4 || ^0.8.0 || ^0.9.0 || ^0.10.0',
  '@emotion/styled': '^11.8.1',
  'date-fns-jalali': '^2.13.0-0 || ^3.2.0-0 || ^4.0.0-0'

where you have '@mui/material': '^5.15.14 || ^6.0.0 || ^7.0.0',.

That means that @mui/x-date-pickers@8.0.0 accepts @mui/material@^7.0.0, which is compliant with your own version of the package

Q: Upload Image in comment of github issue/pull request? A:

You can upload an image in a GitHub comment very easily:

  • Just drag the image into the comment box

  • Or copy the image and paste it there
